account:
Today seems mostly routine from what I have personally seen and heard. I attended the market, reviewed the town accounts, visited my neighbour for tea, and spent the late afternoon available in my office. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. I have now reached home just after seven.

The only unusual news was my neighbour's report of rumours about a celebration or changes to the bridge. They had seen no evidence, and said the baker knew of no celebration. I have no confirmation of either rumour and do not know who started them or what purpose they might serve. The neighbour reported no dockside concerns.

My secretary spent considerable effort confirming the tea location, eventually hearing directly from the neighbour that tea is at the cottage at (16, -60, 105) at three each day. That appears to be ordinary scheduling work, not evidence of anything suspicious. The secretary also said they would go to the mill this evening to ask about concerns for tomorrow's grain inspection. I have not yet heard the result. I do not know of any incoming correspondence awaiting attention or where it would be kept.

The baker was seen putting bread into the market stall this morning, and the neighbour reported fresh bread being stocked and the innkeeper tending supplies. Those sound like normal provisioning. I also noticed a lantern placed in the town hall earlier, but I do not know who placed it or why beyond its apparent use for lighting. Nothing I know presently establishes a special event or a bridge project.
